source_text: Οὐκοῦν νοεῖτε, τέκνα εὐφροσύνης, ὅτι πάντα ὁ καλὸς κύριος προεφανέρωσεν ἡμῖν, ἵνα γνῶμεν, ᾧ κατὰ πάντα εὐχαριστοῦντες ὀφείλομεν αἰνεῖν. εἰ οὖν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, ὢν κύριος καὶ μέλλων κρίνειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, ἔπαθεν, ἵνα ἡ πληγὴ αὐτοῦ ζωοποιήσῃ ἡμᾶς: πιστεύσωμεν, ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἠδύνατο παθεῖν εἰ μὴ δἰ ἡμᾶς. ἀλλὰ καὶ σταυρωθεὶς ἐποτίζετο ὄξει καὶ χολῇ. ἀκούσατε, πῶς περὶ τούτου πεφανέρωκαν οἱ ἱερεῖς τοῦ ναοῦ. γεγραμμένης ἐντολῆς: Ὃς ἂν μὴ νηστεύσῃ τὴν νηστείαν, θανάτῳ ἐξολεθρευθήσεται, ἐνετείλατο κύριος, ἐπεὶ καὶ αὐτὸς ὑπὲρ τῶν ἡμετέρων ἁμαρτιῶν ἔμελλεν τὸ σκεῦος τοῦ πνεύματος προσφέρειν θυσίαν, ἵνα καὶ ὁ τύπος ὁ γενόμενος ἐπὶ Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ προσενεχθέντος ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τελεσθῇ. τί οὖν λέγει ἐν τῷ προφήτῃ; Καὶ φαγέτωσαν ἐκ τοῦ τράγου τοῦ προσφερομένου τῇ νηστείᾳ ὑπὲρ πασῶν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν. προσέχετε ἀκριβῶς: Καὶ φαγέτωσαν οἱ ἱερεῖς μόνοι πάντες τὸ ἔντερον ἄπλυτον μετὰ ὄξους. πρὸς τί ; ἐπειδὴ ἐμὲ ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν μέλλοντα τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ καινοῦ προσφέρειν τὴν σάρκα μου μέλλετε ποτίζειν χολὴν μετὰ ὄξους, φάγετε ὑμεῖς μόνοι, τοῦ λαοῦ νηστεύοντος καὶ κοπτομένου ἐπὶ σάκκου καὶ σποδοῦ. ἵνα δείξῃ, ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν παθεῖν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν. ἃ ἐνετείλατο, προσέχετε: Λάβετε δύο τράγους καλοὺς καὶ ὁμοίους καὶ προσενέγκατε, καὶ λαβέτω ὁ ἱερεὺς τὸν ἔνα εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν. τὸν δὲ ἕνα τί ποιήσωσιν; Ἐπικατάρατος, φησιν, ὁ εἷς. προσέχετε, πῶς ὁ τύπος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ φανεροῦται: Καὶ ἐμπτύσατε πάντες καὶ κατακεντήσατε καὶ περίθετε τὸ ἔριον τὸ κόκκινον περὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὕτως εἰς ἔρημον βληθήτω. καὶ ὅταν γένηται οὕτως, ἄγει ὁ βαστάζων τὸν τράγον εἰς τὴν ἔρημον καὶ ἀφαιρεῖ τὸ ἔριον καὶ ἐπιτίθησιν αὐτὸ ἐπὶ φρύγανον τὸ λεγόμενον ῥαχήλ, οὗ καὶ τοὺς βλαστοὺς εἰώθαμεν τρώγειν ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ εὑρίσκοντες: οὕτω μόνης τῆς ῥαχοῦς οἱ καρποὶ γλυκεῖς εἰσιν. τί οὖν τοῦτό ἐστιν; προσέχετε: Τὸν μὲν ἕνα ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον, τὸν δὲ ἕνα ἐπικατάρατον, καὶ ὅτι τὸν ἐπικατάρατον ἐστεφανωμένον; ἐπειδὴ ὄψονται αὐτὸν τότε τῇ ἠμέρᾳ τὸν ποδήρη ἔχοντα τὸν κόκκινον περὶ τὴν σάρκα καὶ ἐροῦσιν: Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν, ὅν ποτε ἡμεῖς ἐσταυρώσαμεν ἐξουθενήσαντες καὶ κατακεντήσαντες καὶ ἐμπτύσαντες; ἀληθῶς οὗτος ἦν, ὁ τότε λέγων ἑαυτὸν υἱὸν θεοῦ εἶναι. πῶς γὰρ ὅμοιος ἐκείνῳ; εἰς τοῦτο ὁμοίους τοὺς τράγους, καλούς, ἴσους, ἵνα, ὅταν ἴδωσιν αὐτὸν τότε ἐρχόμενον, ἐκπλαγῶσιν ἐπὶ τῇ ὁμοιότητι τοῦ τράγου. οὐκοῦν ἴδε τὸν τύπον τοῦ μέλλοντος πάσχειν Ἰησοῦ. τί δέ, ὅτι τὸ ἔριον μέσον τῶν ἀκανθῶν τιθέασιν; τύπος ἐστὶν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ θέμενος, ὅτι ὃς ἐὰν θέλῃ τὸ ἔριον ἆραι τὸ κόκκινον, δεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ παθεῖν διὰ τὸ εἶναι φοβερὰν τὴν ἄκανθαν, καὶ θλιβέντα κυριεῦσαι αὐτοῦ. οὕτω, φησίν, οἱ θέλοντές με ἰδεῖν καὶ ἅψασθαί μου τῆς βασιλείας ὀφείλουσιν θλιβέντες καὶ παθόντες λαβεῖν με.
pass_a_gloss: So understand, children of joy, that the good Lord has revealed all things to us, so that we may know to whom we owe thanks, praising. If the Son of God, being Lord and about to judge the living and the dead, suffered, so that His wound may give life to us: let us believe that the Son of God was not able to suffer if not for us. But also, having been crucified, He was given vinegar and gall to drink. Hear how the priests of the temple revealed this. A written command: Whoever does not fast the fast, will be destroyed by death, the Lord commanded, since He Himself was about to offer the vessel of the Spirit as a sacrifice for our sins, so that the type that happened with Isaac, who was led to the altar, may be fulfilled. What does He say in the prophet? And let them eat from the goat that is offered for the fast for all sins. Pay attention carefully: And let the priests alone eat all the intestines, unwashed, with vinegar. Why? Since I, who am about to offer My flesh for the sins of My new people, you are going to give Me vinegar and gall to drink, eat you alone, while the people fast and mourn in sackcloth and ashes. So that He may show that He must suffer at their hands. What He commanded, pay attention: Take two fine and similar goats and offer them, and let the priest take one as a whole burnt offering for sins. And what shall they do with the other? Cursed, He says, is the one. Pay attention, how the type of Jesus is revealed: And let them all spit and strike and put the scarlet wool around its head, and so let it be thrown into the wilderness. And when this happens, the one carrying the goat leads it into the wilderness and removes the wool and puts it on a plant called Rachel, on which we were accustomed to eating the shoots in the field: thus, the fruits of this plant alone are sweet. What is this, then? Pay attention: One on the altar, the other cursed, and why the cursed one is crowned? Since they will see Him then on that day, the one with the scarlet around His flesh, and they will say: Is this not the one we crucified, despising and striking and spitting on? Truly, this was the one who said He was the Son of God. How is He similar to that one? The goats are similar, fine, equal, so that when they see Him coming then, they may be amazed at the similarity of the goat. So, behold the type of Jesus who is about to suffer. And what about the fact that they put the wool among the thorns? It is a type of Jesus placed in the church, that whoever wants to take the scarlet wool must suffer much because the thorn is fearful, and to overcome it is to be oppressed. So, He says, those who want to see Me and touch My kingdom must, being oppressed and having suffered, take Me.

choices.why: referring to the Son of God

pass_b_english: Now understand this, children of joy: the good Lord has revealed everything to us so that we may know the One to whom we owe thanks, praising Him in all things. If the Son of God, who is Lord and will judge the living and the dead, suffered so that His wound might give life to us, let us believe that the Son of God could not have suffered unless it was for us. He was also crucified and given vinegar and gall to drink. Listen to how the priests of the temple foreshadowed this. There is a written command: 'Whoever does not fast the fast shall be destroyed by death.' The Lord commanded this, because He Himself was about to offer the vessel of the Spirit as a sacrifice for our sins, so that the type that occurred with Isaac when he was brought to the altar might be fulfilled. What does He say in the prophet? 'Let them eat of the goat that is offered for the fast for all sins.' Pay close attention: 'Let the priests alone eat all the entrails, unwashed, with vinegar.' Why? 'Since I am about to offer My flesh for the sins of My new people, you are going to give Me vinegar and gall to drink; eat it yourselves alone, while the people fast and mourn in sackcloth and ashes,' so that He may show that He must suffer at their hands. Now pay attention to what He commanded: 'Take two goats, fine and alike, and offer them, and let the priest take the one as a whole burnt offering for sins.' And what shall they do with the other? 'Cursed, He says, is the one.' Pay attention to how the type of Jesus is revealed: 'And let them all spit on it and pierce it and put the scarlet wool around its head, and so let it be thrown into the wilderness.' And when this happens, the one carrying the goat leads it into the wilderness, removes the wool, and puts it on a plant called Rachel, whose shoots we are accustomed to eat in the field; thus the fruits of this plant alone are sweet. What does this mean? Pay attention: One goat is on the altar, the other is cursed, and why is the cursed one crowned? Because they will see Him then on that day, the One wearing the scarlet around His flesh, and they will say: 'Is this not the One whom we crucified, despising and piercing and spitting on? Truly this was the One who then said He was the Son of God.' How is He similar to that goat? The goats are similar, fine, equal, so that when they see Him coming then, they may be amazed at the similarity of the goat. So, behold the type of Jesus who is about to suffer. And why do they put the wool among the thorns? It is a type of Jesus placed in the church, that whoever wants to take the scarlet wool must suffer much because the thorn is fearful, and to overcome it is to be oppressed. So, He says, those who want to see Me and touch My kingdom must, being oppressed and having suffered, take Me. (Leviticus 16:20-22)
